# Purpose

I lock scope here before the literature review, umbrella plan, and Ethix application. This note is one page of decisions and open points. It does not replace the protocol.

**Status:** Draft — awaiting sign-off by responsible researcher.

# Population and setting

- **Population:** Adults (≥18 years) who undergo planned surgery under anaesthesia in Sweden.
- **Setting:** Swedish hospital perioperative and anaesthesia care. Mixed surgical categories (aligning with the ICD-10 groups in the Ethix draft).
- **Unit of analysis:** The surgical episode and linked preoperative assessment period, unless a sub-study states otherwise.
- **Inclusion (working):** Patients with sufficient chart and structured perioperative data for the planned analyses.
- **Exclusion (working):** Episodes with no usable preoperative record or missing outcome linkage.

**Open:** Exact hospital(s)/region(s) and final inclusion rules after data access is confirmed.

# Data sources and access

| Source | Content | Role |
|--------|---------|------|
| Electronic health records (journal) | History, examination notes, assessments, comorbidity | Chart review; AI-assisted extraction in controlled environment |
| Structured perioperative data | Anaesthesia records, surgery codes, timings, labs where available | Variables and outcomes |
| Registers (as approved) | Outcomes, diagnoses, mortality, readmission | Validation and follow-up |

- **Access route (to confirm):** Research agreement with data controller(s); register extracts via approved pathways (e.g. regional database, SWEDEPOR/Surgery/quality registers where applicable).
- **Ethix alignment:** Register and journal data (`§10.1`); sensitive health data; no direct participant contact in the current Ethix draft (`§9.1` Nej).

**Open:** Named registers, legal basis for each source, and data processor agreements.

# Design

| Track | Guideline | Status |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| **Primary:** Observational chart-based study | SPIROS | In scope for ethics application and first analyses |
| **Contingent:** Trial of AI-supported vs usual preoperative pathway | SPIRIT 2025 | Not started; separate protocol and amendment if pursued |

**Primary design elements:**

- Retrospective and/or prospective observational cohort using routinely collected data.
- Development and evaluation of AI-assisted methods to structure preoperative fitness signals and draft management suggestions.
- Association analyses between patient-level variables and perioperative outcomes.
- No change to clinical care solely because of this research phase.

# Outcome families

## Primary (for association and feasibility work)

1. **Major perioperative morbidity** — composite or domain-specific (cardiac, pulmonary, renal, infectious, bleeding) as data allow.
2. **Critical care escalation** — unplanned ICU/HDU admission or equivalent.
3. **Mortality** — in-hospital and/or 30-day where follow-up exists.

## Secondary

1. Length of stay and readmission.
2. **Method performance** — accuracy/completeness of chart extraction vs human reference (subset).
3. **Plan quality** — structured review of AI-drafted suggestions against guideline criteria (no autonomous use in care).

Exact definitions and codes will be fixed in the statistical analysis plan after the literature review.

# AI processing boundary

- AI and agents are **assistive only**. A licensed clinician remains accountable for any clinical decision.
- I will not deploy autonomous patient-facing or clinician-facing decision support in care during this phase.
- Identifiable chart text stays in approved environments. External APIs (e.g. OpenRouter) only with explicit approval and contractual controls; prefer local open-weight models for identifiable data where feasible.
- I will log prompts, model versions, and outputs as allowed by ethics and the data controller.
- I will disclose AI-assisted writing and research methods (see `docs/ai-transparency.md` and the attribution ledger).
